title: The change-classification system
text: Classification trialdiff deliberately boring auditable: every change row long change register ([as_register()]); every category comes explicit [td_rule()]; first matching rule (priority) sets primary category, matching rules retained category_all; change carries plain-language reason. machine learning hidden scoring.

title: The change-classification system
text: rule predicate register. context contains dataset name, keys sets subjects present cut.
code: age_rule <- td_rule(   name = "age_change",   label = "Age change",   priority = 1L,   test = function(register, context) {     register$record_type == "modified" & register$variable == "AGE"   },   reason = function(register, context) {     sprintf("Age changed for %s.", register$.subject)   } )  custom <- classify_changes(   diff,   rules = c(list(age_rule), td_default_rules()) ) custom$register$category[custom$register$variable == "AGE"] #> [1] NA            NA            NA            "age_change"  "age_change"  #> [6] "type_change"

title: The change-classification system
text: Rules evaluated ascending priority order. matters one rule apply. example, AVAL derived variable value can transition missing non-missing. Missingness transitions higher priority generic derived-variable rule, actionable review: change rule matches marked unclassified surfaced report item requiring manual review, rule set can never silently hide change.
code: old <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S1", "S2"), AVAL = c(NA, 5)) new <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S1", "S2"), AVAL = c(3, NA)) classified_missing <- classify_changes(compare_cut(old, new, by = "USUBJID",                                                     dataset = "ADLB")) classified_missing$modified[, c("USUBJID", "variable", "change", "category")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   USUBJID variable change           category         #>   <chr>   <chr>    <chr>            <chr>            #> 1 S1      AVAL     missing_to_value missing_to_value #> 2 S2      AVAL     value_to_missing value_to_missing

title: trialdiff and the existing ecosystem
text: novelty comparison. combination : clinical change taxonomy; explicit, user-declared lineage datasets, variables, analyses outputs; transparent, policy-driven impact assessment distinguishes “definitely”, “potentially” “unlikely”, refuses claim statistical impact without rerun; reporting lists exactly programmer statistician must review. package pharmaverse currently occupies position. See project proposal proposal/ full gap analysis roadmap.

title: Lineage and impact assessment
text: Lineage directed graph. edge -> means “depends ”. Node identifiers follow simple convention: Edges can carry condition, example TRT01P == "Drug ", recorded transparency evaluated package.
code: library(trialdiff) lineage <- define_lineage(   lineage_edge("ADSL.TRT01P", "ADLB.TRT01P", relationship = "groups_by"),   lineage_edge("ADLB.AVAL", "ADLB.BASE", relationship = "derives"),   lineage_edge("ADLB.AVAL", "ADLB.CHG", relationship = "derives"),   lineage_edge("ADLB.AVAL", "MMRM", relationship = "models"),   lineage_edge("MMRM", "Table_14_2_1", relationship = "reports") ) lineage #>  #> ── trialdiff lineage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> 5 edges, 7 nodes #> analysis: 1 #> output: 1 #> variable: 5

title: Lineage and impact assessment
text: trace_dependencies() performs breadth-first traversal returns path taken, every flag can explained. Upstream tracing also supported:
code: trace_dependencies(lineage, from = "ADLB.AVAL") #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   node         node_type depth path                            edge_relationship #>   <chr>        <chr>     <int> <chr>                           <chr>             #> 1 ADLB.BASE    variable      1 ADLB.AVAL -> ADLB.BASE          derives           #> 2 ADLB.CHG     variable      1 ADLB.AVAL -> ADLB.CHG           derives           #> 3 MMRM         analysis      1 ADLB.AVAL -> MMRM               models            #> 4 Table_14_2_1 output        2 ADLB.AVAL -> MMRM -> Table_14_… reports trace_dependencies(lineage, from = "Table_14_2_1", direction = "upstream") #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   node      node_type depth path                              edge_relationship #>   <chr>     <chr>     <int> <chr>                             <chr>             #> 1 MMRM      analysis      1 Table_14_2_1 -> MMRM              reports           #> 2 ADLB.AVAL variable      2 Table_14_2_1 -> MMRM -> ADLB.AVAL models

title: Lineage and impact assessment
text: assess_impact() maps classified changes onto lineage graph. reached node graded given rationale. grading rules exposed [impact_policy()], study team can agree document conventions.
code: classified <- classify_changes(   compare_cut(adsl_cut1, adsl_cut2, by = "USUBJID", dataset = "ADSL") ) impact <- assess_impact(classified, adsl_adlb_lineage) impact$impacts[, c("node", "node_type", "level", "depth", "requires_rerun")] #> # A tibble: 8 × 5 #>   node                     node_type level                depth requires_rerun #>   <chr>                    <chr>     <chr>                <int> <lgl>          #> 1 ADLB.TRT01P              variable  definitely_affected      1 FALSE          #> 2 ADSL.TRT01A              variable  definitely_affected      1 FALSE          #> 3 Efficacy_Set             analysis  potentially_affected     1 TRUE           #> 4 Safety_Set               analysis  potentially_affected     1 TRUE           #> 5 Lab_Summary_By_Treatment analysis  potentially_affected     2 TRUE           #> 6 MMRM                     analysis  potentially_affected     2 TRUE           #> 7 Table_14_2_1             output    potentially_affected     3 TRUE           #> 8 Table_14_2_2             output    potentially_affected     3 TRUE impact_policy() #>  #> ── trialdiff impact policy #> value_direct: "definitely_affected" #> value_indirect: "potentially_affected" #> record: "potentially_affected" #> schema: "potentially_affected" #> label: "unlikely" #> max_depth: Inf

title: Getting started with trialdiff
text: Clinical trial datasets regenerated many times study. two data cuts, observations added, removed corrected, derivations change, metadata evolves. Generic tools diffdf waldo can tell two datasets differ. trialdiff answers clinical-programming question comes next: changed, change represent, downstream analyses outputs might affected? trialdiff organised five layers, usable : Compare - [compare_cut()] Classify - [classify_changes()] Trace - [define_lineage()], [trace_dependencies()] Assess - [assess_impact()] Report - [report_diff()] five layers deterministic rule-based. Nothing inferred opaque model, statistical significance ever claimed.

title: Clinical Trial Data-Cut Change Detection and Impact Assessment
text: diffdf (waldo) excellent low-level comparison tools, trialdiff deliberately reinvent . trialdiff adds layers specific clinical programming: clinical change taxonomy (new subject, new visit, corrected value, missingness transitions, derived-variable change, treatment-assignment change, metadata change, …); explicit lineage datasets, variables, analyses outputs; auditable impact assessment documented policy; review reports name objects programmer statistician must check. can even delegate low-level comparison : compare_cut(..., backend = "diffdf") uses diffdf detect differences translates result tdiff object.

Added "diffdf" comparison backend compare_cut(), delegates value comparison  package translates output tdiff object (schema comparison remains built ). as_register() now coerces key columns character, fixing failure key columns character. title: trialdiff 0.1.0
text: First tagged release. Five composable layers: compare, classify, trace, assess report. compare_cut() compares two data cuts clinical dataset reports added, removed modified observations plus schema changes. classify_changes() applies transparent, prioritised rules produce clinical change taxonomy. define_lineage() trace_dependencies() build query lineage graph. assess_impact() grades downstream impact definitely/potentially/unlikely. report_diff() produces HTML, Quarto, JSON list reports. Synthetic ADSL/ADLB data cuts example lineage included.
